title: [CQ-V10] Changed code architecture rules
description:
Objective: Select versioned project-native import/dependency/schema checks against actual changed code.

Deliverable: Changed code architecture rules. This is task V10 of the approved full CQ rollout; consume this contract, not the whole reference document.

Scope boundaries: implement this behavior and its regression tests only. Later activation, other platform/client consumers and other task behaviors remain out of scope unless named here. Approved full CQ-01–CQ-08 rollout from the interactive implementation plan (2026-10-24). CQ-01 is already landed. Use original Moe source; daemon owns state, wrappers own host Git writes. User selected Moe-provisioned LOCAL Linux VMs (not cloud CI), coding/QA and checks isolated, and exact designated LOCAL BRANCH delivery. Strong profile stays disabled until isolation, evidence and client gates pass. Preserve legacy behavior and existing dirty bytes. Never directly edit .moe. No second revision authority, scheduler, graph database or native memory database.

Verification command (fresh, exit0 required): cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test

Dependency aliases (wired by Moe task ids after import): V04, C05.
definitionOfDone: Forbidden import fails even if plan prose follows rails.
Dynamic uncertainty is surfaced, not automatically deleted.
Checks use protected definitions and immutable candidate.
Fresh verification `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` exits0 and its output is supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

implementationPlan.description:
TESTS FIRST (red). Build on the LANDED V10a module packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/architectureRules.ts (task-2cd62d2c): parseArchitectureRules, extractImports, resolveImport, evaluateArchitecture. Adapt to its landed names. If V04 (task-a9d1a74d) lands a dispatch hook for required checks, note it, but keep this task's surface a plain CLI command.

Create packages/moe-daemon/src/commands/checkArchitecture.test.ts.
- Use real temp Git repos, with GIT_* masked and fixed identities, as in repositorySource.test.ts.
- The fixture is a base commit plus a CANDIDATE commit whose first parent is base, mirroring the wrapper's frozen candidate (commit-tree tree -p base).
- arch.json holds rule 'state-no-tools': from ['src/state'], forbid ['src/tools'].
- Assert the exact exit code and the exact JSON report, never truthiness.

Cases:
- A1, DoD1. The candidate adds `import { t } from '../tools/t.js'` to src/state/s.ts. The plan prose for it passes checkPlanRails with the project's rails (util/rails.ts). The check still exits 1, reporting a violation {ruleId:'state-no-tools', file:'src/state/s.ts', line, specifier, resolved:'src/tools/t.ts'}.
- A2, DoD2. A changed file has `await import(name)`: exit 2, outcome 'inconclusive', with the dynamic-import entry surfaced in `uncertain`.
- A3, DoD3 (immutable candidate). The forbidden import exists only as an uncommitted worktree edit: exit 0. Only committed bytes are read.
- A4, DoD3 (protected definitions). A task whose executionContract.requiredChecks is {id:'arch', command:'node packages/moe-daemon/dist/index.js check-architecture --rules arch.json', configs:['arch.json'], scripts:['packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/architectureRules.ts','packages/moe-daemon/src/commands/checkArchitecture.ts']}. A candidate whose protectedEntries change arch.json gives evaluateDeliveryEvidence 'protected-check-changed:arch.json' under deliveryPolicy 'local-branch'. Reuse V01's requiredChecks.delivery.test.ts helpers.
- A5, selection. A candidate touching only docs/ gives selectedRules [] and exit 0.
- A6, errors: a missing or malformed arch.json at the tree, an unresolvable revision, and a changed JS/TS file over the source cap. Each gives exit 2 with a named reason, and never 0.

Implement packages/moe-daemon/src/commands/checkArchitecture.ts:
`export async function runCheckArchitecture(argv: string[], cwd: string): Promise<{ exitCode: 0 | 1 | 2; report: object }>`.

Error handling: every Git, read or parse failure gives exitCode 2 with report.reason. It never throws, and never gives exit 0 on uncertainty.

Arguments: `--rules <repo-path>` (required), `--base <rev>` and `--tree <rev>`.
- tree defaults to HEAD^{commit} of cwd: the frozen candidate in the gate workspace.
- base defaults to tree^1, the candidate's baseRevision.

Use only bounded, read-only Git through openProjectGit (util/cachedPlanPaths.ts), and NEVER read the worktree:
- `diff-tree -r -z --no-renames --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --name-status <base> <tree>` gives the A, M and T paths to scan; deleted paths are skipped.
- `ls-tree -r -z --name-only --full-tree <tree>` gives treePaths.
- Read the rules and the changed .ts, .tsx, .js, .mjs and .cjs files at the tree through readRepositorySource (context/repositorySource.ts), in batches of at most 32 queries. Any non-'served' item gives exit 2, with an `unreadable` entry.
- parseArchitectureRules, then evaluateArchitecture.

Exit 0 means passed, 1 failed, 2 inconclusive or unavailable. Print the report as one JSON line on stdout, so the runner's output tail carries it.

One adversarial self-review of this task's diff, the last step (load adversarial-self-review). Check:
- Can a candidate pass by editing arch.json or the checker itself? A4 must refuse it through V01 protected drift; a plain run of the command alone cannot see that.
- Path traversal or option injection through --rules, --base or --tree (use --end-of-options and reject a leading '-').
- A huge diff: buffer caps give exit 2.
- Gitlinks or symlinks among the changed paths: refused, never followed.
- A rename seen as delete plus add with --no-renames.
- No .moe edits, no Git writes, no forbidden-pattern tokens.
- verified-local is not enabled.
Write the handoff memory, noting that dispatching the command as a required check is V04's job.

comments.author: architect-e4b7eee0
comments.content:
V10a (task-2cd62d2c) plan rev 1 is approved. It keeps the documented interface exactly, plus three contract details that V10 should handle:
1. evaluateArchitecture fails closed with INVALID_INPUT ('changed[i].path') on a non-normalized or duplicate changed path. Wrap the call so the error maps to exit 2 with a named reason.
2. Pass EVERY diff-tree A/M/T path in `changed`, so selectedRules reflects all changes. Text is read only for .ts/.tsx/.js/.mjs/.cjs, so '' is fine for other paths.
3. Uncertainty reasons are exactly dynamic-import, non-literal-require and unresolved-relative. A relative import that escapes the repo root or matches no tree path is unresolved-relative. Specifiers containing backslashes are resolved with '/' separators. Result objects have a fixed key order, so the JSON report is deterministic.

comments.author: worker-73c29a03
comments.content:
From CQ-V10a, round 2 (worker-73c29a03): what V10 must handle or document about the engine it consumes (architectureRules.ts, landed in 7664bbba).

Fail-closed refusals: map each of these INVALID_INPUT refusals to exit 2.
- parseArchitectureRules refuses with context.field one of: architectureRules, version, <unknownKey>, rules, rules[i], rules[i].<key>, rules[i].id, rules[i].from[j], rules[i].forbid[j], rules[i].reason.
- evaluateArchitecture refuses with changed[i].path when a path is not normalized, is a duplicate, is absolute, contains '..', has a drive letter, or is over 500 characters.

Open bugs, both filed in BACKLOG with dependsOn V10a:
1. task-16628bef427b426aa9d8fc6ac1d19534 (HIGH). A lexer desync hides imports on LATER lines, with no uncertainty. The plan assumed "line-local recovery"; that is false whenever template or `/* */` state flips.
   - Triggers: a division misread as a regex after `}`, postfix ++/-- or TS `!` (QA's advisory 1, which also covers the same-line case); a regex read as division after `extends` or `export default`; an Annex-B `<!--` comment in CJS; a backtick in TSX text.
   - Six repros are in the task. Do not treat 'passed' as trusted until this is resolved.
2. task-54dc3d385ef542a08a0a8e9aa2ce8969 (MEDIUM, QA's advisory 2). resolveImport tries joined+ext before the directory index for '.', '..', a trailing '/' and a trailing '/.'. A decoy sibling src/state.ts makes `'../state/'` resolve to the decoy, so the outcome is 'passed' instead of 'failed'.

Accepted residuals to document:
- JSX text is lexed as code.
- A regex after a non-control `)` reads as division.
- Path aliases are treated as external.
- Runtime indirection (an aliased require, createRequire) is out of reach.
- .mts, .cts and .jsx files are not scanned.
- A target that exists only as a .d.ts is unresolved.

comments.author: architect-32ff5555
comments.content:
Architect note, 2026-10-30: task-16628bef (plan rev 1, now WORKING; this task depends on it) widens ImportUncertainty.reason with 'ambiguous-syntax'.

The new reason marks a line inside a multi-line template-text or block-comment region that would import if it were code. It is reported after an earlier lexing ambiguity: a code-position '/', '<!--' or '-->' with a backtick, '/*', or a '}' inside a substitution later on its line, or a JSX-like '<'.

evaluateArchitecture still maps any uncertainty to 'inconclusive', so V10 should surface 'ambiguous-syntax' as a named exit-2 reason next to the existing three, and its docs should explain it. Same-line misreads stay an accepted V10a residual, so document them too.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1. One task holding the engine plus the wiring. About 450 lines, over the cap. Split: the pure engine became V10a (task-2cd62d2c, order 8.4, with the exact interface in its description), and V10 is the CLI and candidate wiring.
2. A new dependency (dependency-cruiser or eslint-plugin-import). Rejected: the daemon deliberately ships few dependencies, and a small import scanner is enough for project rules.
3. Daemon-side execution of the check. Rejected: the daemon never runs commands. The runner's frozen gate runs required checks, so the check is a CLI command evaluated on the frozen commit (HEAD versus HEAD^), and its rules and sources are protected through V01 requiredChecks configs and scripts.
4. Reading the rules at base instead of the tree. Rejected: V01 protected drift already refuses a candidate that changed arch.json, so the tree read matches what V01 protects.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- CLI commands are a switch in src/index.ts (`case 'doctor'` calls commands/doctor.ts runDoctor).
- Bounded Git: util/cachedPlanPaths.ts openProjectGit. Committed-bytes reads: context/repositorySource.ts readRepositorySource (64 KiB cap, at most 32 queries).
- V01 protection: delivery/policy.ts protectedDrift and evaluateDeliveryEvidence. Test helpers are in delivery/requiredChecks.delivery.test.ts.
- Rails text checks: util/rails.ts checkPlanRails, which only checks plan prose; that gap is why DoD1 exists.
- The wrapper's frozen candidate commit = commit-tree(tree, -p base), so HEAD^ is the candidate's baseRevision in the gate workspace.
planningNotes.risks:
- V04 and V10a are unplanned or unlanded: adapt to their names.
- The wrapper maps a nonzero exit to code-failure, so inconclusive is a non-pass and is surfaced in the output tail. A distinct 'inconclusive' outcome needs wrapper mapping, which is out of scope.
- index.ts is a busy file: keep the edit to the one case.
- Size is at most 400 net lines.
